title: CTS Radical Christianity — Unit 13: Capstone — Turning the World Upside Down

blocks.en: 📖 Radical Christianity: The Ten Commandments of Jesus — Unit 13 (Capstone): Turning the World Upside Down
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Cristianismo Radical: Los Diez Mandamientos de Jesús — Unidad 13 (Final): Trastornando el Mundo

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "These who have turned the world upside down have come here too." — Acts 17:6 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Estos que trastornan el mundo entero también han venido acá." — Hechos 17:6 (RVG)

blocks.en: 1. A Phrase Meant as an Insult
blocks.es_reference: 1. Una Frase Dicha como Insulto

blocks.en: Acts 17:6 (NKJV): "These who have turned the world upside down have come here too."
blocks.es_reference: Hechos 17:6 (RVG): "Estos que trastornan el mundo entero también han venido acá."

blocks.en: When the gospel reached Thessalonica, the people who hated it dragged Paul's hosts before the rulers and spat out a complaint that has echoed ever since: these men "have turned the world upside down." It was meant as an accusation. It became one of the highest compliments ever paid to the church. A handful of ordinary disciples had so disturbed the settled order of a Roman city that the authorities took official notice. That is the note on which this course must end. You have spent twelve units learning what it means to follow Jesus radically; this final unit asks the question those twelve were always driving toward — what happens when such disciples are turned loose on the world?
blocks.es_reference: Cuando el evangelio llegó a Tesalónica, los que lo odiaban arrastraron a los anfitriones de Pablo ante los gobernantes y escupieron una queja que ha resonado desde entonces: estos hombres "trastornan el mundo entero." Se dijo como acusación. Llegó a ser uno de los más altos elogios jamás dados a la iglesia. Un puñado de discípulos comunes había perturbado de tal modo el orden establecido de una ciudad romana que las autoridades tomaron nota oficial. En esa nota debe terminar este curso. Usted ha pasado doce unidades aprendiendo qué significa seguir a Jesús radicalmente; esta unidad final hace la pregunta a la que aquellas doce siempre apuntaban — ¿qué sucede cuando tales discípulos son soltados sobre el mundo?

blocks.en: There is an old story of an eccentric open-air preacher who took this very text and announced his sermon in three blunt points: first, the world is wrong side up; second, the world must be turned upside down; third, we are the ones to set it right. In his plain way he had captured the whole purpose of the gospel. The world as it stands is not right side up at all — it is upside down, with self on the throne and God at the margins, the proud exalted and the humble despised. To turn such a world "upside down" is in fact to turn it right side up. The radical disciple is not a vandal of the social order but God's chosen instrument for setting a fallen world back on its feet.
blocks.es_reference: Hay una vieja historia de un excéntrico predicador al aire libre que tomó este mismo texto y anunció su sermón en tres puntos rotundos: primero, el mundo está al revés; segundo, el mundo debe ser puesto de cabeza; tercero, nosotros somos los que hemos de enderezarlo. En su manera sencilla había captado todo el propósito del evangelio. El mundo tal como está no está derecho en absoluto — está al revés, con el yo en el trono y Dios al margen, los soberbios exaltados y los humildes despreciados. Poner tal mundo "de cabeza" es en realidad enderezarlo. El discípulo radical no es un vándalo del orden social sino el instrumento escogido de Dios para volver a poner en pie a un mundo caído.

blocks.en: 2. You Cannot Do It in Your Own Strength
blocks.es_reference: 2. No Se Puede Hacer en Su Propia Fuerza

blocks.en: Before we speak of how disciples turn the world upside down, we must be honest about where the power comes from, because it does not come from us. Look again at the men accused in Thessalonica, and remember what they had been only weeks before. These were the same disciples who ran away when Jesus was arrested, who hid behind locked doors, whose boldest member denied his Lord to a servant girl. Cowards do not turn the world upside down. Something had happened to them.
blocks.es_reference: Antes de hablar de cómo los discípulos trastornan el mundo, debemos ser honestos sobre de dónde viene el poder, porque no viene de nosotros. Mire de nuevo a los hombres acusados en Tesalónica, y recuerde lo que habían sido apenas semanas antes. Eran los mismos discípulos que huyeron cuando Jesús fue arrestado, que se escondieron tras puertas cerradas, cuyo miembro más valiente negó a su Señor ante una criada. Los cobardes no trastornan el mundo. Algo les había sucedido.

blocks.en: Two things had happened. First, they met the risen Christ. The resurrection took a band of frightened, defeated men and made them fearless witnesses; Peter, who had cowered before a servant, soon stood in the streets of Jerusalem and preached to thousands. Then, at Pentecost, the Holy Spirit was poured out, and what had been a timid huddle became a flame — so full of God that onlookers thought them drunk at nine in the morning.
blocks.es_reference: Dos cosas habían sucedido. Primero, se encontraron con el Cristo resucitado. La resurrección tomó a un grupo de hombres asustados y derrotados y los hizo testigos sin temor; Pedro, que se había acobardado ante una criada, pronto se puso de pie en las calles de Jerusalén y predicó a miles. Luego, en Pentecostés, el Espíritu Santo fue derramado, y lo que había sido un grupito tímido se volvió una llama — tan lleno de Dios que los que miraban pensaron que estaban borrachos a las nueve de la mañana.

blocks.en: Acts 1:8 (NKJV): "You shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me..."
blocks.es_reference: Hechos 1:8 (RVG): "Recibiréis poder, cuando haya venido sobre vosotros el Espíritu Santo, y me seréis testigos..."

blocks.en: The lesson is plain: the church turns the world upside down only by the upside-down power of a crucified and risen Lord and the fullness of His Spirit. Attempt it in your own strength and you will only wear yourself out. Go in His power, and a few ordinary people can shake a city. This is why a capstone on world-changing must begin on its knees and not with a strategy.
blocks.es_reference: La lección es clara: la iglesia trastorna el mundo solo por el poder al revés de un Señor crucificado y resucitado y por la plenitud de su Espíritu. Inténtelo en su propia fuerza y solo se agotará. Vaya en el poder de Él, y unos pocos comunes pueden sacudir una ciudad. Por eso una unidad final sobre cambiar el mundo debe empezar de rodillas y no con una estrategia.

blocks.en: 3. The Witness of a Changed Life
blocks.es_reference: 3. El Testimonio de una Vida Cambiada

blocks.en: How does such power become visible? Often not first in what a disciple says, but in what a disciple is. Witnessing is not only the words of your mouth; it is also the testimony of your life. A Christian whose life is indistinguishable from the world's is like an albino zebra among horses — he may know what he is on the inside, but to everyone watching he looks no different from the rest. The disciple who turns the world upside down is one whose life is visibly, unmistakably set apart.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cómo se hace visible tal poder? A menudo no primero en lo que un discípulo dice, sino en lo que un discípulo es. Testificar no es solo las palabras de su boca; es también el testimonio de su vida. Un cristiano cuya vida es indistinguible de la del mundo es como una cebra albina entre caballos — quizá sepa lo que es por dentro, pero para todos los que miran no se ve diferente de los demás. El discípulo que trastorna el mundo es aquel cuya vida está visible e inconfundiblemente apartada.

blocks.en:
Jim's Last Words: I knew a man named Jim who had a serious blood condition. He knew that he was dying. Some time before his death, Jim had sought me out because he wanted to make sure that he had salvation. We talked about his relationship with Christ and the assurance of eternal life.

Later, as his condition worsened, I was with him when he died. He was at peace. As I remember it, the last words he spoke were, "I'll soon be with the Lord."

A short time later there was a gasp. Those of us with him knew that he had taken his last breath.

I had watched a man move from wanting to make sure that he was ready to meet the Lord to facing death with the quiet confidence that he soon would. His faith did not remove death, but it changed the way he faced it.
blocks.es_reference:
Las últimas palabras de Jim: Conocí a un hombre llamado Jim que tenía una grave enfermedad de la sangre. Sabía que se estaba muriendo. Algún tiempo antes de su muerte, Jim me había buscado porque quería asegurarse de tener la salvación. Hablamos de su relación con Cristo y de la seguridad de la vida eterna.

Más tarde, cuando su condición empeoró, yo estaba con él cuando murió. Estaba en paz. Según lo recuerdo, las últimas palabras que dijo fueron: "Pronto estaré con el Señor."

Poco después se oyó un suspiro entrecortado. Los que estábamos con él supimos que había dado su último aliento.

Había visto a un hombre pasar de querer asegurarse de que estaba listo para encontrarse con el Señor a enfrentar la muerte con la serena confianza de que pronto lo haría. Su fe no le quitó la muerte, pero cambió la manera en que la enfrentó.

blocks.en: The same thing happens in ordinary kindness. A man spent months patiently helping a refugee family get food and work, longing to tell them about Jesus but unable to cross the language barrier — until one day the refugee asked him, "Is your God like you? If He is, I want to know Him." The man thought he had failed to share the gospel; in truth he had been preaching it the whole time, with the one sermon the world cannot argue with: a life filled with Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Lo mismo sucede en la bondad común. Un hombre pasó meses ayudando con paciencia a una familia refugiada a conseguir comida y trabajo, anhelando hablarles de Jesús pero sin poder cruzar la barrera del idioma — hasta que un día el refugiado le preguntó: "¿Es tu Dios como tú? Si lo es, quiero conocerlo." El hombre creyó haber fracasado en compartir el evangelio; en verdad lo había estado predicando todo el tiempo, con el único sermón que el mundo no puede refutar: una vida llena de Cristo.

blocks.en: 4. Radical the Way John Was
blocks.es_reference: 4. Radical como lo Fue Juan

blocks.en: A world-turning life will always look a little strange to the world. Consider John the Baptist. He wore camel's hair and ate locusts; he lived apart, devoted to God, refusing the distractions everyone else accepted as normal. People no doubt thought him eccentric, even crazy. But John was not odd for the sake of being odd; he was set apart unto God, and out of that set-apart life came a message that shook a nation: "Repent." He walked up to the comfortable religion of his day and said, in effect, you are in sin; get right with God.
blocks.es_reference: Una vida que trastorna el mundo siempre le parecerá un poco extraña al mundo. Considere a Juan el Bautista. Vestía de pelo de camello y comía langostas; vivía apartado, consagrado a Dios, rehusando las distracciones que todos los demás aceptaban como normales. Sin duda lo creían excéntrico, hasta loco. Pero Juan no era raro por ser raro; estaba apartado para Dios, y de esa vida apartada salió un mensaje que sacudió a una nación: "Arrepentíos." Se acercó a la religión cómoda de su día y dijo, en efecto: estáis en pecado; poneos a bien con Dios.

blocks.en: God is still calling out John the Baptists — people who will get holy and even get a little "crazy" in whatever wilderness He has placed them: a home, a job, a campus, a neighborhood. The disciple who would turn the world upside down must be willing to be thought strange. You cannot blend in and stand out at the same time. The cost of being different is real, but it is the very thing that makes the witness visible.
blocks.es_reference: Dios todavía está llamando a Juanes Bautistas — personas que se pongan santas y hasta un poco "locas" en cualquier desierto donde Él las haya puesto: un hogar, un trabajo, una escuela, un vecindario. El discípulo que quiera trastornar el mundo debe estar dispuesto a ser tenido por extraño. No se puede confundir con la multitud y destacar al mismo tiempo. El costo de ser diferente es real, pero es lo mismo que hace visible el testimonio.

blocks.en: 5. The Whole Course Was for This
blocks.es_reference: 5. Todo el Curso Fue para Esto

blocks.en: This capstone does not introduce a new subject; it gathers up everything you have already learned. Every "Be" of this course was preparing you to turn the world upside down. A disciple who is genuinely generous, who truly trusts God, who is faithful in prayer, who is kind to the difficult, who quietly makes other disciples — that disciple is, by the mere fact of such a life, a disturbing presence in a selfish world. Radical living is not loud; it is simply different, and difference is what overturns.
blocks.es_reference: Esta unidad final no introduce un tema nuevo; recoge todo lo que usted ya ha aprendido. Cada "Sed" de este curso lo estaba preparando para trastornar el mundo. Un discípulo que es genuinamente generoso, que de veras confía en Dios, que es fiel en la oración, que es bondadoso con el difícil, que calladamente hace otros discípulos — ese discípulo es, por el mero hecho de tal vida, una presencia perturbadora en un mundo egoísta. El vivir radical no es ruidoso; es sencillamente diferente, y la diferencia es lo que trastorna.

blocks.en: Ordinary radicals: A young dishwasher, barely scraping by, walked home and gathered the Christmas presents from under his own tree to give to a boatload of penniless refugees who had washed ashore cold and wet. Centuries earlier, a wealthy young widow named Olympias gave away her entire fortune to the poor, the sick, and the imprisoned, even buying slaves in order to set them free. Neither overthrew a government. Both turned a small corner of the world upside down by living as if the kingdom of God were already true — because for them it was.
blocks.es_reference: Radicales comunes: Un joven lavaplatos, apenas sobreviviendo, caminó a casa y recogió los regalos de Navidad de debajo de su propio árbol para dárselos a un grupo de refugiados sin un centavo que habían llegado a la orilla fríos y mojados. Siglos antes, una joven viuda adinerada llamada Olimpia regaló toda su fortuna a los pobres, los enfermos, y los presos, comprando hasta esclavos para ponerlos en libertad. Ninguno derrocó a un gobierno. Ambos trastornaron un pequeño rincón del mundo viviendo como si el reino de Dios ya fuera verdad — porque para ellos lo era.

blocks.en: Do not despise the smallness of your own obedience. The world is turned over not by a few spectacular heroes but by many ordinary disciples doing radical, Christlike things in the unremarkable places God has put them. The twelve units behind you were never academic exercises. They were the forming of a life that the world cannot ignore.
blocks.es_reference: No desprecie la pequeñez de su propia obediencia. El mundo no se trastorna por unos pocos héroes espectaculares sino por muchos discípulos comunes que hacen cosas radicales y semejantes a Cristo en los lugares poco notables donde Dios los ha puesto. Las doce unidades tras de usted nunca fueron ejercicios académicos. Fueron la formación de una vida que el mundo no puede ignorar.

blocks.en: 6. Expect the World to Be Upset
blocks.es_reference: 6. Espere que el Mundo se Moleste

blocks.en: We should be clear-eyed about what comes next, because the same passage that praises world-turners also shows their cost. In Thessalonica, Paul and Silas reasoned in the synagogue and persuaded a number of people. But others were unconvinced and complained that the preaching was disruptive and upsetting; they stirred up the city, dragged the believers before the authorities, and the two missionaries had to flee by night. Notice the charge: the gospel was "disruptive." Of course it was. A message that calls the proud to repent and dethrones every false god will always upset somebody.
blocks.es_reference: Debemos ver con claridad lo que viene después, porque el mismo pasaje que elogia a los que trastornan el mundo también muestra su costo. En Tesalónica, Pablo y Silas razonaron en la sinagoga y persuadieron a varios. Pero otros no se convencieron y se quejaron de que la predicación era perturbadora y molesta; alborotaron la ciudad, arrastraron a los creyentes ante las autoridades, y los dos misioneros tuvieron que huir de noche. Note la acusación: el evangelio era "perturbador." Por supuesto que lo era. Un mensaje que llama al soberbio a arrepentirse y destrona a todo dios falso siempre molestará a alguien.

blocks.en: So do not be surprised when the world pushes back. Opposition is not a sign that you have failed; it is often a sign that the gospel is actually landing. And notice what Paul and Silas did when one city rejected them: they merely moved on to Berea and reasoned and converted a few more. They did not quit; they relocated and kept going. The command of our Lord still stands: "Go into all the world" — even if the world gets a little upset.
blocks.es_reference: Así que no se sorprenda cuando el mundo lo rechace. La oposición no es señal de que ha fracasado; con frecuencia es señal de que el evangelio de veras está dando en el blanco. Y note lo que hicieron Pablo y Silas cuando una ciudad los rechazó: sencillamente siguieron a Berea y razonaron y convirtieron a unos pocos más. No se rindieron; se trasladaron y siguieron adelante. El mandato de nuestro Señor sigue en pie: "Id por todo el mundo" — aunque el mundo se moleste un poco.

blocks.en: 7. Obey God Rather Than Men
blocks.es_reference: 7. Obedecer a Dios Antes que a los Hombres

blocks.en: Acts 5:29 (NKJV): "We ought to obey God rather than men."
blocks.es_reference: Hechos 5:29 (RVG): "Es necesario obedecer a Dios antes que a los hombres."

blocks.en: There comes a point where the powers that be order the disciple to stop — to keep his faith private, to quit speaking that name, to confine religion safely inside a building. We feel the pressure of it even now, in a culture that increasingly treats public witness as an offense; there are stories of a child told she may not read her Bible or pray during recess because someone found it "disruptive," while far worse things go unchallenged. The first proclaimers met this very command. Hauled before the council and ordered to stop teaching in the name of Jesus, they answered plainly: we must obey God rather than men.
blocks.es_reference: Llega un punto en que los poderes que gobiernan le ordenan al discípulo que se detenga — que guarde su fe en privado, que deje de hablar ese nombre, que confine la religión a salvo dentro de un edificio. Sentimos esa presión aun ahora, en una cultura que cada vez más trata el testimonio público como una ofensa; hay historias de una niña a quien se le dijo que no podía leer su Biblia ni orar durante el recreo porque a alguien le pareció "perturbador," mientras cosas mucho peores quedan sin reproche. Los primeros proclamadores enfrentaron este mismo mandato. Llevados ante el concilio y ordenados a dejar de enseñar en el nombre de Jesús, respondieron con sencillez: es necesario obedecer a Dios antes que a los hombres.

blocks.en: That is the courage the capstone requires. Christians have never lived through a season when everyone encouraged them to proclaim Christ; there have always been those who give strict orders not to continue. The disciple who turns the world upside down is simply one who, when God and men give opposite commands, has already decided whom he will obey. He is respectful, not reckless — but he does not fall silent.
blocks.es_reference: Ése es el valor que requiere esta unidad final. Los cristianos nunca han vivido una temporada en que todos los animaran a proclamar a Cristo; siempre ha habido quienes dan órdenes estrictas de no continuar. El discípulo que trastorna el mundo es sencillamente aquel que, cuando Dios y los hombres dan mandatos opuestos, ya ha decidido a quién obedecerá. Es respetuoso, no temerario — pero no se calla.

blocks.en: 8. Setting the World Right Side Up
blocks.es_reference: 8. Enderezar el Mundo

blocks.en: What does a turned-over world actually look like? Rarely a sudden political upheaval; usually the quiet, cumulative, finally explosive effect of changed lives. The Day of Pentecost ended with three thousand new believers; within a generation the gospel had run from Jerusalem to the edges of the empire. Again and again in history the same thing has happened: a handful of people pray until heaven opens, and a whole region is transformed, crime falls, and lives are remade — from Pentecost itself to the awakenings that have swept nations since. This is the gospel doing what the eccentric preacher said: making a wrong-side-up world right.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cómo se ve en realidad un mundo trastornado? Rara vez una súbita revuelta política; por lo general el efecto callado, acumulativo, y finalmente explosivo de vidas cambiadas. El Día de Pentecostés terminó con tres mil nuevos creyentes; en una generación el evangelio había corrido de Jerusalén a los confines del imperio. Una y otra vez en la historia ha sucedido lo mismo: un puñado de personas ora hasta que el cielo se abre, y toda una región es transformada, el crimen cae, y las vidas son rehechas — desde Pentecostés mismo hasta los avivamientos que han barrido naciones desde entonces. Esto es el evangelio haciendo lo que dijo el excéntrico predicador: enderezar un mundo que está al revés.

blocks.en: And it works by multiplication. Turned-over people turn over others. A disciple who has been set right helps set another right, who helps set another, until what began with a few ordinary believers spreads further than anyone could have planned. You are not asked to overturn the world single-handedly. You are asked to be one faithful link in a chain God intends never to stop.
blocks.es_reference: Y obra por multiplicación. La gente trastornada trastorna a otros. Un discípulo que ha sido enderezado ayuda a enderezar a otro, que ayuda a enderezar a otro, hasta que lo que empezó con unos pocos creyentes comunes se esparce más lejos de lo que nadie pudo planear. No se le pide que trastorne el mundo usted solo. Se le pide que sea un eslabón fiel en una cadena que Dios quiere que nunca se detenga.

blocks.en: 9. We Are the Ones
blocks.es_reference: 9. Nosotros Somos los Que

blocks.en: So we come to the end of the course, and the end is really a beginning. The men of Thessalonica meant "these who have turned the world upside down" as a charge to be answered in court. Let it be the ambition our lives answer for. You have learned to be generous, to trust, to pray, to be kind, to make disciples — not so that you could collect a certificate, but so that you could be turned loose. A diploma marks the end of study; a commission marks the beginning of a mission.
blocks.es_reference: Así llegamos al final del curso, y el final es en realidad un comienzo. Los hombres de Tesalónica dijeron "estos que trastornan el mundo entero" como un cargo que responder ante el tribunal. Que sea la ambición que nuestras vidas respondan. Usted ha aprendido a ser generoso, a confiar, a orar, a ser bondadoso, a hacer discípulos — no para poder recoger un certificado, sino para poder ser soltado. Un diploma marca el fin del estudio; una comisión marca el comienzo de una misión.

blocks.en: The honest question, then, is whether it could ever be said of you and your church: these have turned the world upside down. It will not be said of spectators. It will be said of ordinary disciples who, in the power of the risen Christ and the fullness of His Spirit, refuse to blend in, expect to be misunderstood, obey God rather than men, and go — even if the world gets a little upset. The world is wrong side up. It must be turned upside down. And by His grace, we are the ones He has sent to set it right.
blocks.es_reference: La pregunta honesta, entonces, es si alguna vez podría decirse de usted y de su iglesia: estos han trastornado el mundo. No se dirá de espectadores. Se dirá de discípulos comunes que, en el poder del Cristo resucitado y la plenitud de su Espíritu, rehúsan confundirse con la multitud, esperan ser malentendidos, obedecen a Dios antes que a los hombres, y van — aunque el mundo se moleste un poco. El mundo está al revés. Debe ser puesto de cabeza. Y por su gracia, nosotros somos los que Él ha enviado a enderezarlo.

mc.stem: The accusation 'these have turned the world upside down' was first made against believers in which city?
mc.why: In Thessalonica (Acts 17), opponents dragged Paul's hosts before the rulers, charging that these men had turned the world upside down.

mc.stem: As originally spoken, the phrase 'turned the world upside down' was meant as —
mc.why: It was meant as an accusation, yet it became one of the highest compliments ever paid to the church.

mc.stem: According to the preacher's three points, the world as it now stands is —
options: Wrong side up — self on the throne, God at the margin
mc.why: The world as it stands is upside down, with self enthroned and God pushed to the margin; the gospel turns it right side up.

mc.stem: To turn such a world 'upside down' is in fact to —
mc.why: Because the world is already upside down, turning it 'upside down' actually sets it right side up; the disciple sets a fallen world back on its feet.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, the power to turn the world upside down comes from —
options: The risen Christ and the fullness of His Spirit
mc.why: The power is not ours; the church turns the world upside down only by the risen Lord and the fullness of His Spirit.

mc.stem: Only weeks before Thessalonica, these same disciples had been —
options: Frightened men who hid behind locked doors
mc.why: They had been frightened men who hid; cowards do not turn the world upside down — something had happened to them.

mc.stem: What two things transformed the timid disciples into fearless witnesses?
options: Meeting the risen Christ and the Spirit poured out at Pentecost
mc.why: The resurrection made them fearless and Pentecost filled them with the Spirit; together these turned a timid huddle into a flame.

mc.stem: According to Acts 1:8, believers receive power to be witnesses when —
options: The Holy Spirit comes upon them
mc.why: Acts 1:8 ties witnessing power directly to the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the believer.

mc.stem: The lesson says a capstone on world-changing must begin —
options: On its knees, in prayer, not with a strategy
mc.why: Because the power comes from God, the work of changing the world begins on its knees, not with a human strategy.

mc.stem: A Christian whose life is indistinguishable from the world's is compared to —
mc.why: Like an albino zebra among horses, he may know what he is inside, but to onlookers he looks no different from the rest.

mc.stem: The lesson says witnessing is —
options: Not only words but also the testimony of a life
Only the words of your mouth
mc.why: Witnessing is not only what you say but what you are; a changed life is a sermon the world cannot argue with.

mc.stem: As Jim was dying, the last words he spoke, as Dr. Cook remembers them, were —
mc.why: Jim had sought Dr. Cook out to make sure of his salvation; at the end he was at peace, and his last words were "I'll soon be with the Lord." His faith did not remove death, but it changed the way he faced it.

fill.prompt: When the gospel reached ____, opponents complained that these men "have turned the world upside down."
The eccentric open-air preacher's first point was that the world as it stands is ____, with self on the throne and God at the margins.

sa.prompt: Explain the accusation in Acts 17:6 and why a charge meant as an insult became a compliment to the church.
sa.model: In Thessalonica the enemies of the gospel dragged Paul's hosts before the rulers, complaining that these men had turned the world upside down. The words were meant as an accusation — a charge that the preaching was disruptive and upsetting. Yet the complaint accidentally paid the church one of its highest compliments: a handful of ordinary disciples had so disturbed the settled order of a Roman city that the authorities had to take official notice. That is exactly what the gospel is supposed to do. A message that calls the proud to repent and dethrones every false god cannot help unsettling a world built the other way around. So the insult names the very thing every faithful church should hope to be charged with — a community whose witness genuinely disturbs the status quo for the sake of Christ.

sa.prompt: Explain the eccentric preacher's three points and what 'turning the world upside down' really accomplishes.
sa.model: An eccentric open-air preacher once announced this text in three blunt points: the world is wrong side up, the world must be turned upside down, and we are the ones to set it right. In his plain way he had captured the purpose of the gospel. The world as it stands is not right side up at all; it is upside down, with self on the throne and God pushed to the margin, the proud exalted and the humble despised. So to turn such a world 'upside down' is in fact to turn it right side up. The disciple is not a vandal of the social order but God's chosen instrument for setting a fallen world back on its feet. Turning the world upside down, then, is simply the gospel doing its proper work: restoring a world that is living the wrong way up.

sa.prompt: Explain where the power to turn the world upside down comes from, using the resurrection and Pentecost.
sa.model: The power does not come from us. The men accused in Thessalonica were the same disciples who only weeks before had run away when Jesus was arrested and hidden behind locked doors; their boldest member had denied his Lord to a servant girl. Cowards do not turn the world upside down. Two things changed them. First, they met the risen Christ; the resurrection took frightened, defeated men and made them fearless witnesses, so that Peter soon preached to thousands. Second, at Pentecost the Holy Spirit was poured out, and a timid huddle became a flame, so full of God that onlookers thought them drunk at nine in the morning. Acts 1:8 ties it together: power to be witnesses comes when the Spirit comes. The church turns the world upside down only by the risen Lord and the fullness of His Spirit — never in its own strength.

sa.prompt: Explain how a changed life witnesses, using the zebra image and the story of Jim's last words.
sa.model: Witnessing is not only the words of your mouth; it is also the testimony of your life. A Christian whose life is indistinguishable from the world's is like an albino zebra among horses — he may know what he is on the inside, but to everyone watching he looks no different from the rest. The disciple who turns the world upside down is one whose life is visibly, unmistakably set apart. Dr. Cook's friend Jim shows the power of this. Dying of a serious blood condition, Jim first sought him out to make sure of his salvation; at the end he was at peace, and his last words were "I'll soon be with the Lord." Those beside him watched a man move from wanting to be sure he was ready to meet the Lord to facing death with quiet confidence. His faith did not remove death, but it changed the way he faced it — a life filled with Christ is the one sermon the world cannot argue with.

sa.prompt: Explain what made John the Baptist radical and what his example teaches disciples today.
sa.model: John the Baptist wore camel's hair and ate locusts; he lived apart, devoted to God, refusing the distractions everyone else accepted as normal. People surely thought him eccentric, even crazy. But John was not odd for the sake of being odd; he was set apart unto God, and out of that set-apart life came a message that shook a nation: repent. He walked up to the comfortable religion of his day and said, in effect, you are in sin; get right with God. The lesson for disciples today is that a world-turning life will always look a little strange to the world, and God is still calling out John the Baptists — people willing to get holy and even a little 'crazy' in whatever wilderness He has placed them, whether a home, a job, a campus, or a neighborhood. You cannot blend in and stand out at the same time; the cost of being different is the very thing that makes the witness visible.

sa.prompt: Explain how the course's twelve 'Be' themes prepare a disciple to turn the world upside down.
sa.model: This capstone introduces no new subject; it gathers up everything already learned. Every 'Be' of the course was preparing the student to turn the world upside down. A disciple who is genuinely generous, who truly trusts God, who is faithful in prayer, who is kind to the difficult, and who quietly makes other disciples is, by the mere fact of such a life, a disturbing presence in a selfish world. Radical living is not loud; it is simply different, and difference is what overturns. The illustrations prove it: a struggling dishwasher gave away his own Christmas gifts to penniless refugees, and a wealthy widow named Olympias gave her whole fortune to the poor and even bought slaves to free them. Neither overthrew a government, yet both turned a corner of the world upside down by living as if the kingdom were already true. We must not despise the smallness of our own obedience; the world is overturned by many ordinary disciples doing radical, Christlike things where God has placed them.

sa.prompt: Explain why disciples should expect opposition, using Paul and Silas in Thessalonica.
sa.model: The same passage that praises world-turners also shows their cost. In Thessalonica, Paul and Silas reasoned in the synagogue and persuaded a number of people, but others were unconvinced and complained that the preaching was disruptive and upsetting; they stirred up the city, dragged the believers before the authorities, and the missionaries had to flee by night. Notice the charge: the gospel was 'disruptive.' Of course it was — a message that calls the proud to repent and dethrones every false god will always upset somebody. So disciples should not be surprised when the world pushes back; opposition is not a sign of failure but often a sign that the gospel is actually landing. And notice what Paul and Silas did: they did not quit but moved on to Berea and reasoned and converted a few more. The command still stands: go into all the world — even if the world gets a little upset.

sa.prompt: Explain 'we ought to obey God rather than men' (Acts 5:29) and the courage it requires.
sa.model: There comes a point where the powers that be order the disciple to stop — to keep his faith private, to quit speaking that name, to confine religion safely inside a building. We feel that pressure even now in a culture that increasingly treats public witness as an offense. The first proclaimers met this very command: hauled before the council and ordered to stop teaching in the name of Jesus, they answered plainly, we ought to obey God rather than men. That is the courage this capstone requires. Christians have never lived through a season when everyone encouraged them to proclaim Christ; there have always been those who give strict orders not to continue. The disciple who turns the world upside down is simply one who, when God and men give opposite commands, has already settled whom he will obey. He is respectful, not reckless — but he does not fall silent.

sa.prompt: Explain how a turned-over world actually comes about, using changed lives, awakenings, and multiplication.
sa.model: A turned-over world rarely arrives as sudden political upheaval; usually it is the quiet, cumulative, finally explosive effect of changed lives. The Day of Pentecost ended with three thousand new believers, and within a generation the gospel had run from Jerusalem to the edges of the empire. Again and again in history the same thing has happened: a handful of people pray until heaven opens, and a whole region is transformed, crime falls, and lives are remade — from Pentecost itself to the awakenings that have swept nations since. This is the gospel making a wrong-side-up world right. And it works by multiplication: turned-over people turn over others. A disciple who has been set right helps set another right, who helps set another, until what began with a few ordinary believers spreads further than anyone could have planned. No one is asked to overturn the world single-handedly, only to be one faithful link in a chain God intends never to stop.

sa.prompt: Gathering the whole course, summarize what it means to turn the world upside down and why the course ends in a commission, not just a certificate.
sa.model: To turn the world upside down is to let the gospel set a wrong-side-up world right through ordinary disciples living in the power of the risen Christ and the fullness of His Spirit. It means refusing to blend in, witnessing by a changed life and not only words, being radical the way John was, expecting the world to be upset, obeying God rather than men, and going even when it costs — trusting God to multiply changed lives until a whole region is overturned. This is why the course ends in a commission and not merely a certificate. A diploma marks the end of study; a commission marks the beginning of a mission. The student has learned to be generous, to trust, to pray, to be kind, and to make disciples not in order to collect a credential but in order to be turned loose. The honest closing question is whether it could one day be said of us and our church: these have turned the world upside down. It will not be said of spectators, but of ordinary disciples whom He has sent to set the world right.
